ns2:section.sectionText: `TOPIC: Bodies of Knowledge in East Asian History. The two primary aims of this course are to read important works in the history of science and to explore how science was used to produce various bodies of knowledge about people and their environments in East Asia since the seventeenth century. The first half of the semester will focus on old and new research about science within the Qing, Chos?n, and Tokugawa regimes. The second half of the semester will examine more popular uses and interpretations of science in twentieth-century East Asia. This course is organized into two-week units. In the first week of a unit, we will read and discuss an important theoretical work in the history of science. In the following week, we will continue the discussion by focusing on an important empirical study in the histories of science, technology, medicine, or the environment in East Asia. Assessment will be based on engagement in seminar discussions and a semester-long research portfolio project on a topic chosen by the student.
